tickers_to_watch.analysis: Large single-session moves in high-volume names often see partial continuation into the following session as momentum traders add and short-sellers cover. The primary risk is a mean-reversion fade if yesterday's move was news-driven without a fundamental repricing. Watch for volume confirmation in the first 30 minutes — low open volume is an early fade signal.
tickers_to_watch.rationale_plain: Was yesterday's biggest winner — up 12.6% to $178.09.
tickers_to_watch.analysis_plain: When a stock has a really strong day, it often keeps going up the next day too — other traders see the gain and pile in. The risk: if yesterday's jump was just from one piece of news, the stock could give some of those gains back. Watch the first 30 minutes of trading — if not many people are buying, it might fade.

tickers_to_watch.analysis: High-volume declines frequently see follow-through selling as institutional holders reposition and stop-losses trigger below the prior close. A dead-cat bounce is possible intraday but the path of least resistance is lower until a fundamental catalyst appears. Short thesis is best expressed intraday given elevated borrow costs after large single-day drops.
tickers_to_watch.rationale_plain: Was yesterday's biggest loser — down 5.9% to $392.99.
tickers_to_watch.analysis_plain: When a stock falls hard, it often keeps falling the next day — big investors keep selling, and automatic 'sell' orders kick in. It might bounce briefly during the day, but the overall direction is usually down until something good happens. Betting on further declines gets expensive after a big drop, so this is best played carefully and quickly.
